problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}+7y=0,\,t>0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}-3t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+7{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }-3\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+7{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-3\lambda +7] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-3\lambda +7 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve the auxiliary equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +4 & =-3 \\ (\lambda -2)^{2} & =-3 \\ \lambda -2 & =\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =2\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =2\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i}.$

Now, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2+\sqrt{3}\text{i}} & ={t}^{2}{e}^{\text{i}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t}={t}^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)), \\ {t}^{2-\sqrt{3}\text{i}} & ={t}^{2}{e}^{-\text{i}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t}={t}^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =A{t}^{2+\sqrt{3}\text{i}}+B{t}^{2-\sqrt{3}\text{i}} \\  & =A{t}^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t))+B{t}^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)) \\  & =(A+B){t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+\text{i}(A-B){t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite $y(t)$ as 

$$
y(t)={t}^{2}({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)),
$$

where ${c}_{1}=A+B$ and ${c}_{2}=\text{i}(A-B).$
